items.title: "Lipoprotein(a) across coronary plaque phenotypes from high-risk to layered plaque: An OCT analysis from the RELACS registry".
items.abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for coronary artery disease, but its relationship with coronary plaque morphology assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) remains incompletely characterized. To investigate the association between circulating Lp(a) levels and OCT-defined coronary plaque phenotypes using a comprehensive segment-level approach. In this prospective single-center study (RELACS registry; NCT05496790), consecutive patients undergoing intracoronary OCT with available Lp(a) measurements were included. Coronary vessels were divided into 3 mm segments and analyzed for plaque characteristics. Lp(a) was primarily modeled as a continuous variable to assess its association with OCT-defined plaque phenotypes, including high-risk, layered, and fibrous plaques. High-risk plaque was defined as the presence of ≥2 criteria between lipid-rich plaque, thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA), and macrophages. Mixed-effects logistic regression models were used to account for within-patient clustering. A total of 952 coronary segments from 50 patients were analyzed. Increasing Lp(a) levels were significantly associated with multiple features of plaque vulnerability, including TCFA, lipid-rich plaques, macrophages, and microchannels. In the multivariate mixed-effects analysis, higher Lp(a) levels were independently associated with a greater likelihood of high-risk plaque (odds ratios [OR] 1.31, 95% CI 1.16-1.48; P < .001) and layered plaques (OR 1.15, 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .024), whereas an inverse association was observed with fibrous plaques (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.70-1.00; P = .047). Increasing Lp(a) levels were associated with OCT-defined coronary plaque phenotypes related to vulnerability and instability, including high-risk and layered plaques. Given the limited patient-level sample size, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

items.title: [Interventional cardiology in 2035: Towards a precision medicine].
items.abstract: Interventional cardiology has continued to progress over the years. Once limited to coronary procedures, it's now evolving toward structural cardiology. Along technological challenges that will gradually being overcome, multimodal imaging is increasingly being integrated to guide procedures, together with artificial intelligence and data analysis, enabling personalized patient care through a global cardiovascular interventional medicine approach.

items.title: Treatment of calcified coronary lesions with intravascular lithotripsy: experience of a regional French centre.
items.abstract: Coronary intravascular lithotripsy (CIVL) has emerged as a promising technique for modifying severe coronary calcification before stent deployment, yet real-world data are still limited. The present study aimed to evaluate the indications, procedural modalities, and clinical outcomes of CIVL in consecutive real-world patients. We conducted a retrospective analysis of all patients in whom CIVL was attempted between April 2022 and December 2023 at our centre, representing our initial experience with this technique. Demographic, clinical, and procedural data were extracted from electronic medical records. Follow-up data were obtained via telephone contact in patients who survived the index hospitalization without major complications. Seventy patients (mean age 76.9±9.3 years, 78.6% male) with one lesion per patient were included. The most frequent cardiovascular risk factor was hypertension (65.7%). 52.9% of patients presented with acute coronary syndromes; and 25% with chronic coronary syndromes. The mean procedural time was 65.6±28.1minutes, fluoroscopy time 25.7±13.6minutes, and contrast volume 170.3±71.6mL. The left anterior descending artery (44.3%) and right coronary artery (34.3%) were most commonly treated. Proximal lesions constituted 42.9% of the cohort. The mean lithotripsy balloon diameter was 3.3±0.5mm; mean stent diameter 3.4±0.5mm; average number of stents per lesion 1.5±0.7; and total stent length 34.6±18.6mm. In 8.3% of cases, CIVL was used as a bailout strategy for stent underexpansion. Angiographic success was achieved in 92.9% of procedures; one case (1.4%) resulted in coronary perforation. In 5.7% of lesions, the operator could not cross the lesion with the balloon; 2.9% required adjunctive rotational atherectomy. Over follow-up, cardiovascular death occurred in 7.1%, with no documented myocardial infarction, stroke, or target vessel revascularization. In an older, comorbid population, CIVL appears to be an effective and safe strategy for treating heavily calcified coronary lesions, with a high angiographic success rate and acceptable complications. Our findings demonstrate that CIVL can be rapidly and safely integrated into the routine clinical workflow of a regional center, even in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome.

items.title: Cepharanthine-Mediated Sonodynamic Action Induces Robust Mitochondrial Damage Through Regulation of Drp-1 Phosphorylation Against Lung Cancer.
items.abstract: Sonodynamic therapy (SDT), an emerging anti-cancer strategy, utilizes ultrasound (US) to activate sonosensitizers derived from natural products, thereby generating singlet oxygen to destroy tumor cells. Cepharanthine (Cep) is a natural phytomedicine with inherent anti-tumor activity, whose efficacy was significantly enhanced by US discovered in the present work. This study aims to further investigate the specific drug target of Cep relevant to SDT/mitochondria and to evaluate the therapeutic effects of Cep-mediated SDT on lung cancer cells and mice. Our findings revealed that Cep binds to dynamin-related protein 1 (Drp1) and inhibits its phosphorylation through SDT, leading to excessive mitochondrial fission. This disruption resulted in severe mitochondrial oxidative stress and subsequent damage. The critical role of Drp1 in this process was confirmed by rescue experiments, wherein overexpression of Drp1 further amplified Cep SDT-induced mitochondrial damage and mitigated its anti-cancer effects in vitro. Ultimately, this mechanism translated into profound therapeutic outcomes: Cep SDT effectively abolished the proliferation and boosted the apoptosis of lung cancer cells. Furthermore, it exhibited a favorable inhibitory effect on tumor growth in mouse models, underscoring its translational potential. To conclude, Cep binds to Drp1 (functional mediator) within lung cancer cells, upon US application, shifts its phosphorylation balance by decreasing inhibitory and increasing activating modifications. This Drp1 hyperactivation triggers excessive mitochondrial fission, which selectively compromises mitochondrial integrity and results in potent SDT destroying of the cancer cells. Our work provides important insights into phytomedicine-based SDT and represents a pioneering exploratory application.

items.title: One-Year Systolic Blood Pressure and Subsequent Cardiovascular Outcomes After Acute Coronary Syndrome: Insights from a Swiss Prospective Cohort.
items.abstract: Current guidelines recommend targeting systolic blood pressure (SBP) below 130 mmHg in patients at high cardiovascular risk, including after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), although evidence specific to the post-ACS setting remains limited. We evaluated the prognostic value of SBP measured 1 year after ACS on subsequent cardiovascular outcomes. The ELIPS cohort prospectively enrolled ACS patients across four Swiss tertiary-care centers (2009-2017). Patients alive at 1 year with available SBP measurements were included. The association between SBP at 1 year and 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; cardiovascular death, non-fatal stroke/transient ischemic attack, or non-fatal myocardial infarction) was modeled using restricted cubic splines, adjusted for age, sex, renal function, cardiovascular risk factors, index-event type, coronary revascularization, cardiac rehabilitation, heart-failure history, and antihypertensive medication classes. Among 2,074 patients (age 63±12 years; 82% male; 53% STEMI), 229 MACE events occurred over a median follow-up of 4.0 years (2.7 per 100 patient-years). The SBP-MACE relationship was nonlinear and J-shaped (P-non-linearity=0.007), with lowest risk between ∼130 and 140 mmHg (formally estimated nadir 138 mmHg [95%CI 116-152]). Above 140 mmHg, each 5-mmHg increase was associated with a borderline increase in MACE risk (adjusted HR 1.08; 95%CI 1.00-1.17). The pattern was broadly consistent across sex, age and hypertension status, with a possible interaction with diabetes that could not be excluded (P-interaction=0.08). In this large, predominantly male, well-characterized post-ACS cohort, SBP measured 1 year after ACS showed a J-shaped association with cardiovascular risk, with lowest risk at 130-140 mmHg. In patients who had survived one year after an acute coronary syndrome, systolic blood pressure measured one year after an acute coronary syndrome showed a J-shaped association with subsequent cardiovascular risk.In a predominantly male cohort (82%) of 2,074 patients followed for a median of 4 years, the risk of major cardiovascular events was lowest at a systolic blood pressure of approximately 130-140 mmHg, with an estimated nadir of 138 mmHg.The risk curve suggested higher cardiovascular risk at lower systolic blood pressure values and showed a progressive increase in risk above 140 mmHg that was of borderline statistical significance, particularly for stroke or transient ischaemic attack. These findings provide prognostic information but should not be interpreted as defining a treatment target.

items.title: Stromal-myeloid-lymphoid crosstalk in immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in solid tumors.
items.abstract: Despite the remarkable advances in cancer immunotherapy, immune evasion, relapse, and immunotherapy resistance remain major challenges in the fight against solid tumors. These limitations cannot be fully attributed to tumor-intrinsic changes; the interplay between stromal, myeloid, and lymphoid (SML) compartments in the tumor microenvironment (TME) strongly influences tumor response. This review summarizes the current understanding of SML crosstalk and how multicellular interactions control immune exclusion, suppression and immunotherapy resistance. We provide a narrative overview of the recent literature to discuss the spatial organization and functional states of stromal, myeloid, and lymphoid populations and the mechanisms involving chemokine-mediated trafficking, cytokine signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, antigen presentation defects, metabolic competition, hypoxia, and immune checkpoint pathways. The evidence suggests that SML crosstalk creates interconnected regulatory circuits in which stromal remodeling fosters myeloid suppression and lymphoid dysfunction, which in turn increases tumor resistance to therapy. These networks are involved in primary and acquired resistance to immune checkpoint blockade and resistance to adoptive cell therapy, cancer vaccines and oncolytic virus therapy. Still, the evidence is limited by significant tumor heterogeneity, reliance on preclinical studies, and insufficient spatial and longitudinal validation as well as by the lack of standardization of biomarkers predictive of treatment outcomes. Future studies should focus on spatial multi-omics, functional experimental models and prospective clinical studies to delineate causal SML interactions and develop clinically relevant biomarkers. A more comprehensive understanding of SML ecosystem dynamics could provide a basis for more accurate patient stratification and appropriate combination therapies in cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Molecular mechanism of S100A11 inhibiting anti-HCC immune function of NK cells.
items.abstract: To explore the regulatory role and underlying molecular mechanism of S100A11 in the anti-hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) function of natural killer (NK) cells, and to provide a novel target and theoretical basis for optimizing immunotherapy for HCC. The expression of S100A11 was validated in clinical specimens. A stable S100A11-knockdown NK92 cell line was established via lentiviral transfection. CCK-8 assay, cell cytotoxicity assay, flow cytometry, Western blot and other experiments were performed to detect changes in NK cell biological functions and related signaling pathways. An HCC xenograft mouse model was established to verify the antitumor effect in vivo. S100A11 was highly expressed in HCC tissues, and its expression level was positively correlated with pathological differentiation grade. Knockdown of S100A11 significantly enhanced the proliferation, degranulation, cytokine secretion and cytotoxic activity of NK92 cells against HCC cells. Moreover, S100A11 knockdown upregulated the expression of activating receptors and downregulated inhibitory receptors on the surface of NK cells. Mechanistically, S100A11 regulated NK cell functions by suppressing the phosphorylation of key molecules in the MAPK signaling pathway and the endoplasmic reticulum stress pathway. In vivo experiments demonstrated that S100A11-knockdown NK92 cells markedly restrained tumor growth, increased NK cell infiltration in tumor tissues, and caused no obvious hepatic injury. S100A11 inhibits the anti-HCC immune function of NK cells by negatively regulating the MAPK and endoplasmic reticulum stress signaling pathways. Targeting S100A11 can restore the cytotoxic activity of NK cells, which is expected to serve as a novel potential target for precise immunotherapy of HCC.

items.title: Immunotherapy and circulating tumor DNA in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of survival and surveillance outcomes.
items.abstract: Human papillomavirus-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma is biologically distinct, yet the effect of immune checkpoint inhibition and the performance of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) as a biomarker remain undefined. We searched databases through October 2025 for prospective studies of adults with HPV-positive OPSCC that reported survival after immune checkpoint inhibition or plasma ctDNA/ctHPVDNA as a prognostic or surveillance biomarker. Two reviewers performed selection, extraction, ROBINS-I, and GRADE. Hazard ratios were pooled by inverse variance (common-effect; DerSimonian-Laird sensitivity), the two streams separately. Six prospective studies (n = 295 HPV-positive patients) were included; none provided an internal immunotherapy-versus-no-immunotherapy contrast. ctDNA was consistently prognostic: across the three with a within-cohort ctDNA-stratified contrast (k = 3, n = 169), pooled hazard ratios were 0.67 (95% CI 0.57-0.80) for progression-free survival and 0.71 (95% CI 0.60-0.85) for overall survival. Whole-evidence-based estimates were 0.70 (95% CI 0.59-0.83) and 0.74 (95% CI 0.63-0.88), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 63.6% and 67.9%), and are carried by the ctDNA contrasts, holding 89% (PFS) and 81% (OS) of pooled weight. The three studies contributing immunotherapy-associated estimates (k = 3, n = 126) showed no benefit (PFS HR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.58-1.59; OS HR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.62-1.32). Plasma ctDNA/ctHPVDNA performed consistently as a prognostic and surveillance biomarker, with early clearance predicting better survival within treated cohorts. The evidence for prospective immunotherapy is too sparse and imprecise to demonstrate a survival benefit, and the favorable pooled signal should not be attributed to immunotherapy. Randomized, biomarker-stratified trials are required.

items.title: Sterility testing in the era of decentralised cell therapy: Challenges, innovations, and future directions.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapies have transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, yet patients with aggressive, time-sensitive disease remain vulnerable to manufacturing-related treatment delays. Current gold-standard sterility testing under United States Pharmacopoeia (USP) requires a 14-day culture period that is structurally incompatible with the clinical timelines of short shelf-life cell therapy products, positioning sterility assurance as the principal bottleneck to decentralised CAR-T manufacturing. Rapid sterility testing methods have emerged as promising alternatives that may resolve this constraint and expand patient access to treatment. We undertook a narrative review of the literature on sterility testing in cell therapy manufacturing to characterise current methodologies and the translational challenges of microbial detection in cell therapy products. Relevant publications were identified through searches of several biomedical databases, including MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed and Cochrane CENTRAL, supplemented by review of reference lists in relevant articles. Eligible studies reported original data relating to sterility testing in cell therapy products or addressed regulatory, infrastructural or procedural considerations relevant to GMP-compliant or decentralised manufacturing environments. ATP bioluminescence, solid phase cytometry, and PCR-based assays targeting conserved 16S/18S rRNA sequences have emerged as rapid alternatives to compendial methods, delivering substantially shorter turnaround times. However, four translational barriers continue to preclude their widespread integration. First, analytical validation requirements demand matrix-specific performance data generated under actual CAR-T manufacturing conditions. Second, the operational infrastructure demands of decentralised sites, spanning personnel training, equipment qualification, and documentation capacity, often makes such data difficult to generate. Third, regulatory acceptability remains inconsistent across jurisdictions with no harmonised pathway for alternative method approval. Fourth, clinical risk governance is hampered by the absence of standardised protocols for managing discordant results that would support conditional release decisions. In response, we propose a structured three-phase validation framework for the conditional release of CAR-T products using rapid sterility assays, progressing from analytical qualification through bridging and equivalency to conditional release implementation, with defined decision gates at each phase transition. Validating and integrating rapid sterility testing into decentralised CAR-T manufacturing workflows offers a credible route to shorter production lead times and broader access to CAR-T cell therapy. Significant barriers remain, however, most notably regulatory fragmentation and a paucity of real-world validation data that currently preclude widespread adoption. The three-phase validation framework proposed in this review provides a structured pathway for conditional release of CAR-T products using rapid sterility assays, progressing from analytical qualification through bridging and equivalency to conditional release implementation, with defined decision gates at each phase transition. Realising the full potential of this framework requires the field to treat regulatory harmonisation and prospective assay validation as jointly necessary conditions for equitable access to cell and gene therapy.
items.journal: Biologicals : journal of the International Association of Biological Standardization

items.title: Design and discovery of highly potent lysine 27 of histone H3 (H3K27) demethylase inhibitors for the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease.
items.abstract: Lysine specific demethylase 6A/B (KDM6A/B), histone lysine demethylases targeting H3K27me3, have emerged as key regulators of inflammatory gene expression and are increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, there remains a critical need for potent, selective, and cell-active KDM6A/B inhibitors to validate their therapeutic potential in inflammatory diseases like IBD. In this work, we conducted a systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) study based on a lead compound GSK-J4 to improve its cellular inhibitory activity. Among these compounds, compound 39 suppressed H3K27me3 levels with an EC 50 of 0.37 μM and a superior selectivity index (SICC 50 /EC 50 ) of 25.27 against KDM6A/B in cells. Moreover, compound 39 showed high anti-inflammatory activity and significantly downregulated the expression levels of Il1b, Il6 and Tnfα in M1 macrophages. In a dextran sulfate sodium-induced murine colitis model, compound 39 significantly attenuated body weight loss and promoted recovery by reducing inflammatory macrophage populations. Thus, these findings demonstrate that the compound 39 is a promising novel candidate for the treatment of IBD.

items.title: Global Sociodemographic Disparities in the Severity of Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis.
items.abstract: Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) carries high short-term mortality, yet the contribution of sociodemographic factors to disease severity and outcomes is poorly defined. We conducted a prospective cohort study across 30 centers in 14 countries (January 2015-September 2024). We included adults who met National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) criteria for AH. Outcomes included infections, access to liver transplantation (LT), and survival. Mortality was analyzed with Fine-Gray competing-risk models. Among 726 participants (median age, 49 years; 90.1% male), 24.8% had less than secondary education, and 37.6% reported good social support. Severe AH was more frequent in those without secondary education than in those with at least secondary education (97.2% vs. 81.7%; P<0.0001). The 30- and 90-day survival rates were lower among participants without secondary education (66.4% and 50.4%, respectively) than among those with at least secondary education (88.4% and 81.2%, respectively). In adjusted analyses, moderate and good social support were associated with lower mortality (each sHR 0.58, 95% CI, 0.38-0.89 and 0.38-0.94, respectively), as were secondary (sHR 0.48, 95% CI, 0.24-0.97) and tertiary education (sHR 0.44, 95% CI, 0.20-0.97) and corticosteroid use (sHR 0.63, 95% CI, 0.42-0.95). Lower educational attainment and poorer perceived social support were associated with greater AH severity at presentation and higher mortality, independent of clinical risk factors. These findings highlight the need to address social determinants and favor equitable access to evidence-based therapies, including early LT.

items.title: Recurrence of autoimmune liver diseases after liver transplantation: exploratory analysis of a pooled Latin American cohort.
items.abstract: Autoimmune liver diseases (AILDs) are an increasingly frequent indication for liver transplantation in Latin America. Recurrence after transplantation may affect graft function and long-term outcomes; however, recurrence patterns and associated factors remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to describe recurrence after liver transplantation in a pooled cohort of AILDs and to explore factors associated with recurrence, overall survival, and retransplantation. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients with AILDs who underwent liver transplantation between 2005 and 2023. Recurrence was defined using biochemical, serological, and histological criteria. Associations were evaluated using logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses. A total of 154 patients were included, of whom 64 (41.5%) developed recurrence after a median of 49 months (IQR 21.2-91). In the primary analysis, recurrence was associated with elevated pre-transplant ALT and AST levels and a history of acute rejection. In sensitivity analyses, elevated AST levels showed the most consistent association with recurrence. Associations involving ALT were attenuated after subgroup restriction, whereas the association with acute rejection varied across analyses. No significant differences were observed in overall survival or retransplantation rates between patients with and without recurrence. Recurrence after liver transplantation was frequent and varied across autoimmune liver disease subtypes. Elevated pre-transplant AST levels were consistently associated with recurrence across exploratory analyses. Despite the high frequency of recurrence, no significant association was observed with impaired overall survival or increased retransplantation. These findings require confirmation in larger multicenter studies with disease-specific analyses.

items.title: Diagnostic gaps in HCV RNA testing in the era of elimination: a single-center study.
items.abstract: It is essential to identify the current gaps in order to reach hepatitis C virus (HCV) elimination. This study focused on detecting undiagnosed HCV cases, to assess clinic awareness levels in the diagnostic process and explore strategies to decrease the number of undiagnosed cases. Anti-HCV seropositive patients identified at the hospital between 1 January 2022, and 31 December 2023, were retrospectively reviewed. Anti-HCV seropositive patients who did not have an HCV ribonucleic acid (RNA) test done were invited to the hospital, and those who came underwent HCV RNA testing. A total of 78,769 anti-HCV tests were conducted at the hospital, with 555 patients (0.7%) testing positive. HCV RNA testing was requested for 307 (55.3%) of the anti-HCV-positive patients during follow-up visits. The rate of HCV RNA test requests among anti-HCV-positive patients was significantly lower in surgical clinics compared to other clinics that requested HCV RNA testing (p < 0.001). Telephone calls were made to 248 patients who had not undergone HCV RNA testing, of whom 114 (46%) could not be reached. An anti-HCV signal-to-cutoff ratio (S/Co) ratio above 10.38 demonstrated 100% sensitivity and 89% specificity in predicting HCV RNA positivity (AUC: 0.95, p < 0.001). Raising awareness among surgical clinics about HCV diagnosis and developing reflex testing algorithms to enable diagnosis at the patient's first hospital visit will significantly support efforts to eliminate HCV.
items.journal: Journal of infection in developing countries

items.title: A divergent hepatitis A virus lineage in wild western lowland gorillas and central chimpanzees supports localized circulation and expands HAV diversity.
items.abstract: Hepatitis A virus (HAV) is a ubiquitous human pathogen that may cause acute liver disease. Despite the availability of effective vaccines, high prevalence rates are still reported in Southeast Asia and Africa, where sanitation conditions are poor. Although seven genotypes are known, including three in humans, three in non-human primates (NHP), and one recently identified in alpacas, the diversity, ecology, and evolutionary history of HAV remain poorly understood. In a pilot study of virome molecular characterization of wild African apes by using oligonucleotide probes enrichment, HAV sequences were detected in two animals (2/105; 1.9%): one from a western lowland gorilla ( Gorilla gorilla gorilla ) from southern Cameroon, sampled in 2006, and another from a central chimpanzee ( Pan troglodytes troglodytes ) in northeastern Gabon, sampled in 2011, approximately 450 km apart. Two near-full-length viral genomes were successfully reconstructed using specific primer sets that were developed. Phylogenetic analyses revealed that these sequences cluster within the simian HAV clade, forming a distinct cluster closely related to environmental strains from the Sanaga River in Cameroon and South Africa, yet clearly divergent from genotype V sequences (≥15.8% nucleotide divergence in the VP1 protein). Amino acid comparisons identified residues conserved in simian HAVs and, subsequently, only in African HAV strains. These results support the classification of a supplementary African simian genotype, provisionally designated HAV-VIII. HAV-positive samples (13/227; 5.7%) were detected in the same field sites, suggesting localized viral circulation in these populations. Bayesian time-scaled phylogenetic analysis estimated the most recent common ancestor of the human and simian HAV lineages at ~ 2 291 years ago and that of simian lineages at ~ 1900 years ago, with a more recent diversification (~100 years ago) within the identified lineage. This study highlights the presence of HAV in wild ape populations for the first time and also the first HAV detection among NHP species in Central Africa. These findings contribute to our current understanding of the diversity and evolution of HAV and highlight the need to extend surveillance across NHP species to better assess potential zoonotic risks.

items.title: Cytomegalovirus Hepatitis Occurring in a Young Patient With Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome and Pediatric-Onset Autoimmune Hepatitis.
items.abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) hepatitis is rare in patients with autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) on long-term immunosuppression. We report a 28-year-old woman with a history of autoimmune polyglandular syndrome and pediatric-onset AIH who presented with fatigue, fever, and elevated liver enzymes, found to have CMV hepatitis without active AIH. Early initiation of antiviral therapy led to normalization of liver function tests and resolution of viremia. This case highlights the importance of early diagnosis of CMV hepatitis and the therapeutic challenge of treating CMV while also reintroducing immunosuppression for AIH.

items.title: Association of obstructive sleep apnea with pancreatic cancer in high-risk patients under surveillance in CAPS and PCYST cohorts.
items.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has been linked with increased cancer incidence and mortality. We hypothesized that OSA may be a risk factor for neoplastic progression among patients undergoing pancreatic cancer surveillance. Retrospective medical record review of two Johns Hopkins Hospital cohorts undergoing pancreas surveillance; patients with familial/genetic risk enrolled in the Cancer of the Pancreas Screening (CAPS) study and patients with incidentally detected pancreatic cysts, enrolled in the PCYST study. Time-to-progression to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and neoplastic progression (either PDAC, high-grade dysplasia or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor) were compared by OSA status, adjusting for covariates. OSA was diagnosed prior to or during surveillance in 174 (19.5%) of 893 patients in CAPS and 376 (23.7%) of 1585 patients in the PCYST cohort. In the combined cohorts, OSA was associated with increased risk of progression to PDAC (unadjusted HR: 3.12, 95% CI: [1.82, 5.34], p < 0.001). OSA was also associated with male sex, higher BMI, fatty liver, fatty pancreas, diabetes, and history of smoking (all p < 0.01). After covariate adjustment, OSA remained associated with PDAC risk (adjusted HR: 2.56 [1.44, 4.55], p = 0.001). Factors associated with neoplastic progression included OSA (adjusted HR: 1.93 [1.25, 2.97], p = 0.003), increasing age (age-per 5-years adjusted HR: 1.14 [1.05, 1.24], p = 0.003), fatty liver (adjusted HR: 1.76 [1.19, 2.60], p = 0.005), and diabetes (adjusted HR: 1.77 [1.16, 2.71], p = 0.008). Patients undergoing pancreatic surveillance for their familial/genetic risk and/or incidentally detected pancreatic cysts have a greater likelihood of developing pancreatic cancer if they've been diagnosed with OSA.
items.journal: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]

items.title: Uncertainty-aware auto-segmentation enables adaptive radiotherapy planning of liver metastases.
items.abstract: Despite remarkable auto-segmentation performance and growing clinical adoption, models frequently fail to generalize beyond the training distribution. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and validate an uncertainty-aware segmentation pipeline that yields high delineation accuracy for liver cancer patients and reliably identifies safety-critical segmentation imperfections in radiotherapy. Datasets of n = 173 patients with 224 liver metastases were divided into training (n = 100), validation (n = 33), and test (n = 40). Each case included annotated T2-weighted magnetic resonance images. An nnU-Net segmented treatment-relevant organs and provided a margin-extended hepatic mask, which served as input to a second-stage SE-ResUNet for lesion delineation. Uncertainty was approximated via checkpoint ensembling under a cyclic learning-rate schedule, yielding entropy-based uncertainty maps and case-wise uncertainty scores. These guided an adaptive post-inference analysis consisting of (i) detection of potentially missed lesions and (ii) identification of problematic contours. Performance was evaluated on 40 patients (n = 52 lesions) using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), 95%-Hausdorff-Distance (HD95), expected calibration error (ECE), uncertainty coverage, and the correlation between case-wise uncertainty scores and segmentation accuracy. Overall performance across treatment-relevant organs was DSC/HD95 = 0.89/4.8 mm; lesionsegmentation achieved DSC/HD95 = 0.86/4.9 mm. Uncertainty-guided post-processing, triggered in 14/40 cases, recovered 7 initially missed metastases, increasing lesion-level sensitivity from 84.6% (44/52) to 98.1% (51/52). Uncertainty estimates showed good calibration with ECE/uncertainty coverage for organs/lesion of 7.2/93.7% and 7.5/98.3%, and significant correlation between uncertainty/DSC (r = -0.802). The proposed pipeline seamlessly integrates accurate organ/lesion segmentation, interpretable uncertainty, and anatomy-guided post-processing to detect safety-critical segmentation failures and enable trustworthy AI auto-segmentation in clinical routine.
items.journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology

items.title: OTUD7B associates with immune infiltration and pharmacogenomic profiles in hepatocellular carcinoma: An integrative multi-omics analysis.
items.abstract: OTUD7B is a deubiquitinating enzyme involved in ubiquitin-mediated signaling; however, its clinical and biological relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains incompletely understood. This study evaluated the expression, prognostic, functional, immune-related, and pharmacogenomic associations of OTUD7B through an integrative analysis of publicly available datasets. OTUD7B mRNA expression was evaluated in TCGA-LIHC using UALCAN and independently examined in the GSE76427 microarray cohort. Protein expression was assessed using Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium and Human Protein Atlas data. Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed using GEPIA2. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to evaluate overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) after adjustment for age, sex, pathological stage, histological grade, alcohol consumption, HBV status, and HCV status. Gene co-expression and functional enrichment analyses were conducted using LinkedOmics. Associations with immune-cell infiltration, immune-related genes, copy-number alterations, cancer-related pathways, and m6A regulators were examined using TIMER2.0 and GSCA. Pharmacogenomic associations between OTUD7B expression and drug sensitivity were evaluated using CTRP and GDSC datasets. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05, with false discovery rate correction applied where appropriate. OTUD7B mRNA expression was significantly higher in TCGA-LIHC tumors than in normal liver tissues (p < 0.0001), and proteomic and immunohistochemical data supported increased protein expression. However, OTUD7B expression did not differ significantly between primary HCC and adjacent non-tumor tissues in GSE76427 (p = 0.393). High OTUD7B expression was associated with poorer OS in Kaplan-Meier analysis (HR = 1.6, p = 0.014), but this association did not remain significant after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR = 1.14, 95% CI: 0.70-1.85, p = 0.597). No significant adjusted association was observed for DFS (adjusted HR = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.66-1.81, p = 0.740). OTUD7B expression was also correlated with m6A regulators, selected immune-related genes, computationally inferred immune-cell abundance, and pharmacogenomic drug-response profiles. OTUD7B shows cohort-dependent expression and is associated with functional, immune-related, and pharmacogenomic features in HCC. However, its differential expression was not reproduced in GSE76427, and its prognostic association was not retained after multivariable adjustment. These hypothesis-generating findings require validation in independent clinical cohorts and experimental models.

items.title: Tissue-Specific Isolation of Hepatocyte Extracellular Vesicles From Human Plasma Enables Tissue-Resolved Proteomic and miRNA Profiling.
items.abstract: Tissue-specific resolution remains a critical barrier in liquid biopsy for precision medicine. To address this, we developed NEXPLOR (Novel EXtracellular vesicle PopuLation Omics Revealer), an immunoaffinity platform enabling selective enrichment of circulating tissue-specific extracellular vesicles (TS-EVs), demonstrated here for liver-derived hepatocyte-EVs (h-EVs). Through in silico discovery and orthogonal antibody validation across tissues, we identified a four-marker panel (ASGR1, ASGR2, TFR2, SLCO1B1) that selectively enriched hepatocyte EVs without co-capturing the dominant platelet- and leukocyte-EV background. In a clinical cohort of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), non-cancer cirrhosis and healthy donors, NEXPLOR recovered 57% more proteins than bulk EV isolation, with greater reproducibility. By restoring tissue context, h-EVs exposed liver biology that bulk EVs miss, spanning three levels: metabolic pathways (carbon metabolism, HIF-1α signalling, ferroptosis), HCC-defining proteins (PGD, H2AZ1, PRDX5), and progression-tracking candidates (CFB, PCSK9). Small RNA sequencing detected five miRNAs upregulated in HCC versus cirrhosis h-EVs, against 21 in bulk EVs (no overlap); yet only the h-EV miRNAs mapped to HCC-relevant signalling, and hepatocyte-regulatory miR-124-3p appeared exclusively in h-EVs. Together, these results establish tissue-specific EV enrichment as a route to more actionable, multi-omic liquid biopsies in HCC, cirrhosis and other diseases in urgent need of non-invasive biomarkers for patient diagnosis, monitoring and stratification.

items.title: M2 Macrophage-Derived Small Extracellular Vesicle miR-106a-Loaded QCG Hydrogel Targets the RNF128-LXR Pathway to Reprogram Chondrocyte Cholesterol Metabolism for Osteoarthritis Therapy.
items.abstract: This study addresses osteoarthritis (OA), in which dysregulated chondrocyte cholesterol homeostasis and cellular senescence contribute to cartilage degeneration, by developing an inflammation-responsive injectable QCG hydrogel for local delivery of miR-106a-enriched M2 macrophage-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs). The QCG hydrogel was constructed from quaternized chitosan (QCS) and 4-carboxyphenylboronic acid-gelatin (CPBA-gelatin) and loaded with miR-106a-enriched M2-sEVs (QCG@sEV-miR-106a). M2-sEVs were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation and characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and vesicle-associated protein markers. High-throughput miRNA profiling and chondrocyte RNA sequencing identified miR-106a as a candidate regulatory molecule, and RNF128 was confirmed as a direct target by dual-luciferase reporter assay. Functional experiments showed that miR-106a suppresses RNF128, thereby promoting chondrocyte proliferation and extracellular matrix synthesis while attenuating senescence. Exploratory proteomic screening suggested RNF128-associated changes in cholesterol- and lysosome-related processes, whereas independent molecular and functional assays demonstrated that RNF128 promotes LXRα ubiquitination and proteasome-dependent degradation, suppresses LXR signaling, and disrupts cholesterol homeostasis. In a destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM)-induced OA rat model, QCG@sEV-miR-106a showed ROS-responsive release, prolonged intra-articular retention for up to 22 days, reduced cartilage degeneration and matrix loss, improved pain-related behaviors, and favorable short-term biocompatibility. Together, these findings support a local biomaterial delivery strategy in which miR-106a-mediated RNF128 inhibition preserves LXR signaling and cholesterol homeostasis to attenuate OA-associated chondrocyte senescence.
